description:
FOUND s470a5 (Opus) while byte-comparing emission for task #996 half A5.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3, PPI 1.291, PCL at gen v2-700 and at ccdb6b7 alike):

    ./pl2cl $PERL_SUITE_T/op/try.t > /tmp/a.lisp
    ./pl2cl $PERL_SUITE_T/op/try.t > /tmp/b.lisp
    diff /tmp/a.lisp /tmp/b.lisp
    # 170c170
    # <     t :writes-args nil :captures ARRAY(0x64d0d25fcc18))
    # ---
    # >     t :writes-args nil :captures ARRAY(0x57dd15ae1218))

t/opbasic/concat.t is a second instance.  The emitted text carries a PERL
ARRAYREF's default stringification, i.e. a heap address, in the `:captures'
slot of a sub-info form.  Whatever built that form interpolated an arrayref
where it meant to interpolate the list (or a name).

WHY IT MATTERS, beyond the ugliness:
  * it defeats a byte-compare.  tools/emission-ab.pl and tools/corpus-diff.pl
    report these files as DIFF for no reason, and a session then has to
    hand-verify them.  s470a5 had to normalise `ARRAY\(0x[0-9a-f]+\)' out
    before its A/B check could say anything;
  * the module cache is keyed by the emitted text's provenance
    (*pcl-cache-generation* plus the source path); an address in the OUTPUT
    means the same source compiles to two different files, which is exactly
    the kind of thing that makes a cache hit or miss at random;
  * per CLAUDE.md rule 12's spirit, a value that "looks plausible" and is
    actually an address is the silent-wrong shape.

NOT FIXED HERE â it is pre-existing (reproduced on ccdb6b7) and orthogonal to
the sort work.  The fix is presumably one interpolation site: grep the
emitters for `captures' and find the one that stringifies the arrayref
instead of its contents.

=== CLOSED (s470bi): duplicate of #1118 ===
Same bug, found independently the same day from the other end -- A5 met it as
"the byte-compare says DIFF for no reason", s470bi met it as "why does main
differ from itself in an emission A/B".

The cause is #1118, fixed in s470bi: `Pl::CLForm::to_string` keeps a p-let
DECLARATION ENTRY's name and its keyword class on one line and prints the
FACTS tail with `join`, and the branch is shape-keyed -- "a non-ref atom, then
a non-ref keyword atom".  A `p-sub` FACTS PLIST (ir-spec 5.1) fits that shape
exactly, because it begins `:returns :str`.  Claimed as a declaration entry,
the plist's tail went through `join`, and `:captures`'s value is an ARRAY REF
(`['list', CELLS...]`) -- so perl stringified it.  This task's guess ("one
interpolation site; grep the emitters for `captures'") pointed at the emitter;
the emitter was right and the PRINTER was wrong, which is why the grep would
not have found it.

The fix is one added conjunct (a declaration entry's first element is a NAME,
never a keyword) plus a plist layout that breaks between PAIRS.

THIS TASK'S THIRD BULLET UNDERSTATED IT.  The plist was not merely ugly and
not merely a cache-key hazard: `ARRAY(0x...)` reads as TWO CL forms, so the
plist had ODD LENGTH and `%p-check-facts` killed the file at LOAD --
"p-sub: facts of pl-f are not keyword pairs".  Measured casualties on main:
t/op/try.t and t/opbasic/concat.t (the two files named here) plus cpan
YAML::Tiny and Test::Tester::Capture, a whole file each; and on main
`e73038f` it cost perl-tests/eval.t 36 passing rows (128 -> 92, restored to
128/32 on s470bi's tree -- Fable measured it at the merge review).

Guards: `Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t` +4 rows, including "two transpiles are
byte-identical", which is this task's own repro turned into a gate row.
subject: Emission is NONDETERMINISTIC: a Perl arrayref stringification leaks into the :captures slot, so two runs of the SAME compiler differ byte for byte
